title: Standards registry
intent: One list of every standard known to this platform, whether or not the platform uses it, so the gap between known and aligned is visible. Origin owner 2026-09-08: keep a standards file that tracks which standards align with our tool and which do not, and keep improving it. Taken further here (proposed): each row is computed against the knowledge base, the skill contracts and the examples, so the alignment column is measured rather than asserted.

ladder.contract: a skill contract names the standard (E-standard entity, version, sources), so the platform claims it
ladder.researched: research records exist in kb/research.jsonl and no skill contract names it
ladder.known: listed here only, no research record yet: a gap to research, never to invent

positions.adopt: the platform should name it in a contract
positions.hold: named where it is, no wider use planned
positions.watch: too early or too contested to name, re-check at a phase boundary
positions.decline: considered and not adopted, with the reason

standards.name: Agent Client Protocol
standards.why: The harness turn: open a session, prompt, stream, cancel, stop reason. Wire v1 stable for the interactive seam, headless use unsettled. Not the same thing as IBM's Agent Communication Protocol, which merged into A2A.

standards.name: Agent2Agent protocol
standards.why: Hand-off between units and the published task lifecycle (submitted, working, input-required, completed, failed, cancelled). The Agent Card is the discovery document the registry lacks.

standards.name: AG-UI
standards.why: Typed event stream from an agent to a person's surface; cited by human interaction for the watch and steer shape.

standards.name: Agent Skills specification
standards.why: The portable skill directory: SKILL.md frontmatter, references, progressive loading. The 29 skills already fit it; declaring conformance makes them loadable by any harness that reads it.

standards.name: AGENTS.md
standards.why: Repo-level instructions any coding agent reads. The natural human-readable half of the contract mount.

standards.name: AGNTCY Open Agentic Schema Framework
standards.why: Agent schema and directory that overlaps the A2A Agent Card. Unsettled; re-check at the next phase boundary.

standards.name: JSON-RPC 2.0
standards.why: The transport both the Agent Client Protocol and the Model Context Protocol ride on, so one framing serves the harness and the tools. Researched, not yet named in a contract.

standards.name: Model Context Protocol
standards.why: Tool discovery, descriptors and argument checking before a call leaves the unit. Its authorization section pins OAuth 2.1.

standards.name: OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI 3
standards.why: How a REST or event producer describes itself before an intake mapper or a tool descriptor wraps it.

standards.name: OpenAI-compatible completions
standards.why: The wire family most gateways speak. Not a standard; the model-access contract hides it behind a class of model so a caller never names it.

standards.name: OpenTelemetry Protocol
standards.why: Traces, metrics and logs any collector ingests. The backend is swappable because the wire is fixed.

standards.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions
standards.why: The gen_ai attribute set that makes a model call, its tokens and its tool spans comparable across vendors. Pre-stable; OpenInference and OpenLLMetry converge on it.

standards.name: W3C Trace Context
standards.why: traceparent propagation across the doors and the cell boundary. Telemetry pins run ids as explicit attributes, not trace parentage, and still needs the header to correlate.

standards.name: OpenInference and OpenLLMetry conventions
standards.why: Vendor attribute sets for LLM spans. Map them onto the OpenTelemetry GenAI set rather than emit them.

standards.name: OCI Runtime Specification
standards.why: The cell's declared resources and egress. What makes a plain process, Docker, gVisor, Kata and Firecracker one axis of security profile behind one declare, admit, inspect interface.

standards.name: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693)
standards.why: How a delegated agent gets a short-lived, audience-bound mandate instead of a hand-issued credential.

standards.name: SPIFFE workload identity
standards.why: Every unit names itself with an attested identity nobody typed in. Pairs with token exchange for the mandate.

standards.name: OAuth 2.1
standards.why: The authorization flow the Model Context Protocol specification pins for tool servers. The static bearer the tool-access litmus flagged is the gap this closes.

standards.name: Rich Authorization Requests (RFC 9396)
standards.why: A mandate that says exactly which action on which resource until when. The structured form the policy gate can decide on and the ledger can record.

standards.name: in-toto Attestation Framework
standards.why: The statement that binds an artifact to the code version, inputs and actor that produced it.

standards.name: Dead Simple Signing Envelope
standards.why: The envelope an in-toto statement is signed in.

standards.name: SLSA
standards.why: Build provenance levels and the predicate an outside verifier expects.

standards.name: Sigstore (cosign, Rekor, Fulcio)
standards.why: Keyless signing and a transparency log. The maturity closures name a Sigstore-class external verifier as the fix for records the platform calls tamper-proof.

standards.name: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785)
standards.why: Two digests of the same record agree only if the bytes are canonical first.

standards.name: Certificate Transparency v2 (RFC 9162)
standards.why: The Merkle inclusion proof the state seam uses so one record's membership is provable without holding the log.

standards.name: SCITT
standards.why: Transparency for supply-chain statements beyond code. Complements Rekor; not yet stable.

standards.name: C2PA content credentials
standards.body: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
standards.why: Provenance of generated media. Matters only when an artifact leaves the organisation as media.

standards.name: CycloneDX with ML-BOM
standards.why: The bill of materials for a unit: model class, skills, tools and versions, so a run's provenance names what it was built from.

standards.name: JSON Schema 2020-12
standards.why: Every declared shape, from the envelope to a tool's arguments, is checked against one dialect before anything runs.

standards.name: Problem Details (RFC 9457)
standards.why: One typed failure object at every boundary and a closed registry of problem types.

standards.name: CloudEvents
standards.why: The envelope any producer's event becomes before intake sees it.

standards.name: Idempotency-Key header
standards.why: A repeated request becomes one execution and one answer.

standards.name: iCalendar recurrence rules (RFC 5545)
standards.why: When a recurring unit is due, as a pure function of one rule, a time zone and a window.

standards.name: Rego and the OPA decision API
standards.why: A structured request in, a deterministic allow or deny and the deciding rule out, before anything is spent.

standards.name: Cedar
standards.why: The second policy engine behind the same decision API, proving the engine is swappable.

standards.name: Serverless Workflow
standards.why: The only open workflow document spec. Declined: the composition operators stay a closed set of six; record the mapping instead of adopting the document.

standards.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and Agentic Security Initiative
standards.why: The threat categories a reviewer will ask the policy gate and the cell to answer for.

standards.name: MITRE ATLAS
standards.why: Adversarial tactics against AI systems, the vocabulary for a red-team ceremony.

standards.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
standards.why: Management-system language for govern, map, measure, manage. Maps onto ceremonies and the evaluation gate; not a wire standard.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 42001
standards.why: AI management system certification. Relevant when a customer asks for it.

standards.name: EU AI Act
standards.why: Logging and human oversight obligations map onto telemetry and human interaction. Applies only where deployments touch the EU.

implementations.name: Firecracker microVM
implementations.role: the protected cell in unit design; the preferred profile

implementations.name: gVisor, Kata Containers
implementations.role: middle security profiles on the same axis

implementations.name: Docker, containerd, runc
implementations.role: the light profile and the dry-run shape

implementations.name: goose
implementations.role: the harness inside the cell today

implementations.name: Temporal-class executors
implementations.note: pattern with no open specification; cap-durable-execution owns the contract

no_open_standard.note: case sets, baselines and verdicts have tools (Inspect and similar) but no specification; the contract is the platform's own and is marked proposed
checkpoints, resume points and compensation are a pattern; no body publishes a wire or document format
memory items are vendor-specific everywhere; the platform stores opaque records at a pinned snapshot and defers nothing

no_open_standard.area: cell lifecycle beyond start and stop
no_open_standard.note: pause, resume, snapshot and fork have no standard verb set; the ontology's fourteen verbs are the platform's own
